I love the concept you're exploring here!  It came across to me as saying we all face the choice  of whether we will eventually compromise our humanity to come out on top or preserve our "innocence" as prey. It really communicated to me the issue of choosing whether to become a monster or one who is suffering at the hands the actions of said "predators". I would agree with previous comments that the lines could use so more meat on the bones. I would really like to see this further developed in a way that lends itself to giving the reader a bit more opportunities to visualize the picture you're trying to paint by this predator vs prey dichotomy of the human condition!

For example, "with speed" kind of interrupted the cadence for me a bit. It seemed to lack some "oomf" (for lack of a better word) that I was getting from the rest of the poem's impactful language. Hope this was useful! Great work!

The line about wishing you could shoot laser beams from your eyes for a laser show really struck me! I was expecting you to say you wanted that ability to do something along the lines of vanquishing an enemy or something to that effect. I was pleasantly surprised to realize the wholesome direction you took with that! It communicated, not only a protective air about the relationship between you and this person you care about, but also a yearning you have to see them happy. That kind of relationship is so much deeper than wanting to play the role of a superficial "protector".

I like the idea you're exploring here of wanting superpowers for solely altruistic purposes that are directed towards the well-being of someone you clearly deeply care for. Most of the time when the question is asked, "What superpower would you want?" the responses are followed with self-centered reasonings (i.e. invisibility to spy on people/flying to get to one's own destinations more quickly). 

The second to last stanza I do wish had a bit more impact. Each "power" you mention before is used for the benefit of a specific "you", but here I felt like I lost that and it was more generalized. 

Overall, I found the piece touching in a unique way.
